title: When the Hollow Falls Anew
premise: Felix Ravensworth has spent seven years hiding in Hollow Vale, the one valley where magic dies at its borders, believing exile is the only way to survive the storm-calling gift that killed his family. When a prophecy book written a century ago names tonight's date as the night the Hollow King falls anew, Felix is dragged beyond the valley's edge by forces he cannot refuse, into a kingdom where the true king is bound beneath the crown and a usurper wears his face. Guided by a disgraced royal archivist and a child who can hear the bound king's voice, Felix must learn to wield his storm-calling without destroying himself, discovering that his family's death was no accident but the price of a bargain made generations ago. In the end, Felix unbinds the true king not by killing the thing in the crown, but by taking the binding into his own body — surviving it only because the found family he never believed he deserved refuses to let him carry it alone.
about_author: Orsen Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fantasy. They write about inherited burdens and the families we build when blood fails us, usually during storms.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On the eve of his thirtieth birthday, Felix tends his quiet life in Hollow Vale, suppressing the storm that hums beneath his skin. An old peddler arrives selling a book of prophecies; Felix finds his own name and tonight's date inked a century ago. The valley's magic-dead border shudders. Emotional beat: dread cracking open the safety he built.

chapters.title: Ink That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The prophecy's words begin rewriting themselves in real time, and when Felix touches the page the valley's border expels him violently — magic cannot follow him out, but it can throw him. He lands in the kingdom of Veymar, where the sky is the wrong color and criers announce the Hollow King's centennial coronation. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief for the life just lost.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Heresy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Ashvale, a royal archivist stripped of rank for claiming the king is an impostor, finds Felix because the prophecy book now sits in her confiscated collection — and it names him. She shows him the truth: the real King Aldric has been bound beneath the palace for a hundred years while a hollow thing wears his face. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in shared heresy.

chapters.title: A Voice Under the Stones
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Descending into the palace undercrofts, Felix hears a child's voice singing through the walls — Pip, a scullery orphan who alone can hear the bound king. The king's voice recognizes Felix's storm-calling and names his family's old bargain: the Ravensworths were bound to the binding all along. Emotional beat: the shattering revelation that exile was engineered, not chosen.

chapters.title: What the Storm Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with Wren. Felix attempts his first true storm-calling in seven years and nearly kills them both, reliving the night his family died — the night the binding fed on his uncontrolled gift. Wren teaches him that magic in Veymar is not power but debt, every spell a promise collected later. Emotional beat: terror transformed into disciplined purpose.

chapters.title: The Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. During the Hollow King's centennial feast, Pip witnesses the thing in the crown consume a courtier whole to renew itself. Pip's warnings are dismissed as madness until Felix's storm cracks the feast-hall windows in answer to the king's binding strain. The impostor now knows Felix exists. Emotional beat: childhood innocence colliding with horror, and the courage to act anyway.

chapters.title: Bargains Collected
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The impostor's hunters corner them; Wren trades her last archival secret for their escape and learns the binding can only be transferred to a willing storm-caller of Ravensworth blood — a trap set a century ago. Felix, overhearing, begins quietly preparing to sacrifice himself. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of love versus duty.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the deep vault, Felix begins the unbinding ritual as the Hollow King's essence tears at him, demanding his body as its new vessel. The storm inside him rages toward self-destruction — until Pip and Wren break into the vault, anchoring him with their voices, their hands, their stubborn refusal to let him go alone. Emotional beat: climax — the price of survival refused through found family.

chapters.title: A King Made Whole
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. King Aldric rises freed but weakened, the binding's residue scattered between three bearers instead of one. The impostor, unmade, dissolves into the ash it always was. Aldric names Wren his archivist-chancellor and offers Felix anything — and Felix asks only for a home that isn't a cage. Emotional beat: aftermath, exhaustion, and cautious hope.

chapters.title: Where the Hollow Ends
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. One year later, Felix lives in Veymar not as exile but as the king's storm-warden, teaching Pip to read the weather and arguing with Wren over archive catalogues. The prophecy book's final page now shows an unwritten tomorrow. When the first storm of autumn rolls in, Felix calls it gently, and it answers like family. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance transformed into gift.
